outline.section: The Universal Cart is the biggest commerce infrastructure move of 2026
outline.detail: Google's Agent Payments Protocol and Universal Cart represent the most significant commerce infrastructure shift since one-click checkout. A persistent cart that follows users across Search, Gmail, YouTube, and Gemini — with Nike, Sephora, Target, Walmart, and Wayfair already live — is a genuine milestone. UCP at 5,294 stores and growing 30% MoM is not a pilot. This is the new plumbing of agentic commerce. And it has a structural constraint that nobody is writing about.

outline.section: The constraint that defines every platform in the UCP coalition
outline.detail: Search requires a search query. Gmail requires a Gmail session. YouTube requires a video to be playing. Gemini requires a prompt. The Universal Cart is persistent — but the surface it lives on is not. Every UCP participant, from Nike to Wayfair to the AP2 protocol layer itself, activates at exactly the same moment: the instant a user opens a Google product. That moment is not the beginning of the shopping journey. It is already the middle.

outline.section: What D0 commerce means in contrast to UCP's activation model
outline.detail: D0 is the discovery window that opens when a user wakes their device and closes when they open their first app. Glance's five sub-agents — Weather, Trends, Occasion, Physical Stylist, Lifestyle Detective — have already resolved a commerce card by the time the lock screen renders. The product is visible. The Universal Cart has not yet activated. Google AI Mode has not yet launched. The Gemini assistant has not yet received a prompt. D0 is not a competing checkout — it is the surface that precedes every surface in the UCP coalition.

outline.section: The OEM gap in the UCP coalition: why no OEM-embedded surface has joined
outline.detail: The UCP coalition now includes Google, Shopify, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, Nike, Sephora, Target, Walmart, and Wayfair. Every participant operates at the app or browser layer. No OEM-embedded surface has joined — not because the OEM layer is excluded, but because it doesn't need the protocol. Glance is pre-installed at device manufacture with OEM-level pre-consent. It doesn't need a protocol membership to surface products; it needs only a device wake event, which happens 25+ times per day per user.

outline.section: The GTM implication: brands now need a D0 strategy alongside their UCP integration
outline.detail: Brands attending Salesforce Connections (June 3–4, Chicago) and RetailX/IRCE (June 9–11) will be pitched UCP integrations from every direction. The D0 argument is additive: a lockscreen commerce card that surfaces your product before any UCP session begins is not a substitute for Universal Cart membership — it is the discovery event that makes UCP conversion more likely. First-party, no CFAA exposure, 175M devices, zero download required. The UCP integration captures the transaction. D0 captures the intent.

outline.section: What brands should do in the 90 days before UCP reaches 10,000 stores
outline.detail: UCP is growing 30% MoM. At that rate, it reaches 10,000 stores before September. The window to establish D0 discovery as a distinct brand asset — upstream of the UCP transaction layer — is the next 90 days. Brands that treat the lockscreen as a discovery channel now will have first-mover advantage in the pre-UCP window before the protocol becomes the default agentic commerce infrastructure.

outline.section: The structural constraint that unites all three: they all start with a user decision
outline.detail: Amazon Buy-for-Me activates when a user opens the Amazon app or speaks to Alexa. Klarna inside ChatGPT activates when a user submits a product query. Meta Hatch activates when a user scrolls Instagram or opens a DoorDash session. Every agentic checkout in 2026 begins at the same moment: the instant a user expresses intent. That intent expression — the search, the query, the scroll — is itself a moment that commerce infrastructure has no presence before. The race to own checkout assumes a starting gun that has already fired.

outline.section: Discovery ownership: the unclaimed position in the agentic commerce stack
outline.detail: If every major player is racing to own checkout, the upstream position — discovery, the moment before intent is expressed — is structurally unclaimed at the platform layer. Search engines owned discovery for two decades. Social feeds owned discovery for one decade. The agentic era's discovery layer hasn't been built by any of the players currently racing to own checkout. Glance's lockscreen commerce card is not a checkout product. It is a discovery product. The Brand AI Store puts a brand's product AI on the lockscreen before any intent is expressed — ambient, passive, non-interruptive.

outline.section: What the Brand AI Store does that no checkout agent can replicate
outline.detail: Meta Hatch can complete a DoorDash order. Amazon Alexa can execute a Buy-for-Me transaction. Klarna inside ChatGPT can surface a live price and complete a checkout. ideas.intro:
In the two weeks ending May 20, 2026, three of the largest companies in commerce made their most significant agentic bets to date. Amazon killed Rufus and launched 'Alexa for Shopping' — an autonomous agent that completes purchases end-to-end using stored credentials and 12 months of price history. Klarna embedded 100M live products and real-time pricing inside ChatGPT, turning every product query into a potential purchase. Meta's Hatch agent began testing autonomous shopping with DoorDash, Reddit, and Outlook, targeting TikTok Shop's social commerce dominance.

Every one of these announcements is about checkout. Every one of them assumes the purchase journey has already begun.

Amazon Buy-for-Me starts when a user opens Amazon. Klarna in ChatGPT starts when a user types a product query. Meta Hatch starts when a user scrolls a feed. The entire agentic commerce arms race is a race to own the last 30 seconds of a purchase — the completion, the credential, the confirmation.

Nobody is racing to own the first moment. The moment before intent. The moment before the app opens. That moment — D0, the device-wake window — is the unclaimed position in the 2026 commerce stack. And it is the only position Glance occupies at 175M+ device scale.

ideas.hook: The Agent Payments Protocol, Universal Commerce Protocol, and every agentic checkout stack launched in 2026 share a fundamental dependency: they all need user consent at the app layer — and none of them have solved the consent problem the way Glance did at the OEM layer.

Glance's first-party brand partnerships on the lockscreen carry no CFAA (Computer Fraud and Abuse Act) exposure — a structural legal advantage over agent-mediated scraping and third-party data approaches used by checkout agents

outline.section: The consent architecture problem nobody in agentic commerce is solving
outline.detail: Every agentic commerce system launched in 2026 requires a user to grant consent at the app layer: authorize Amazon Alexa to purchase on your behalf, connect your Klarna account to ChatGPT, allow Meta Hatch to access your payment credentials. This is the right design from a privacy standpoint. It is also a significant friction point. The consent step eliminates a meaningful percentage of potential users before the agentic experience begins. And it must be repeated for each new agentic surface. OEM-level pre-consent — consent granted at device manufacture and setup, covering a pre-installed platform — bypasses this friction entirely.

outline.section: How OEM pre-consent works at the device layer: the Glance architecture
outline.detail: Glance is pre-installed by Samsung and Motorola at device manufacture. The consent framework is established during device setup — the initial out-of-box experience — not during an app install or a shopping session. This means Glance has first-party access to the lockscreen surface without requiring a user to download an app, create an account, or authorize a payment agent. The commerce surface is present before any user choice is made about which apps to install or which agents to trust. This is not a dark pattern — it is a structurally different consent model that operates at the OEM layer, not the app layer.

outline.section: The CFAA exposure that checkout agents are accumulating
outline.detail: Autonomous checkout agents that scrape product data, monitor price changes, and execute purchases on third-party merchant sites operate in legally ambiguous territory under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. Amazon's Buy-for-Me navigates this by operating within Amazon's own inventory. Klarna's ChatGPT integration navigates this via direct API partnership. But the broader class of 'browser agent' commerce tools — agents that navigate merchant sites autonomously on a user's behalf — face CFAA exposure that has not been fully litigated. Glance's first-party brand partnerships are explicitly structured to avoid this: brands deploy directly to the Brand AI Store, no scraping, no unauthorized access, clear contractual commerce.

outline.section: The app-install drop-off that pre-installation eliminates
outline.detail: The median drop-off between product discovery and checkout initiation that occurs during app installation is a well-documented conversion killer. A user who discovers a product on a social feed, clicks through to a merchant site, and is prompted to download the merchant app loses interest at rates that vary by category but rarely fall below 50%. Glance's pre-installed lockscreen surface removes this drop-off entirely: the product is surfaced on the lockscreen, the user taps, and the transaction pathway opens without any install event. The D0-to-conversion funnel has no install step because the platform was installed at device manufacture.

outline.section: What agentic protocol designers should learn from the OEM model
outline.detail: The AP2 and UCP coalitions are building the right infrastructure for the app layer. The consent models they're implementing — authorization flows, payment credential vaults, permission scopes — are appropriate for platforms that users choose to install. But there is a parallel architecture that the protocol designers haven't engaged: the OEM-embedded layer, where consent is established at device setup and the commerce surface is present before any app choice is made. IRCE/RetailX (June 9–11) is the right venue to make this argument to platform architects: the agentic commerce stack is missing an OEM tier.

outline.section: The architectural implication: D0 as the pre-protocol discovery layer
outline.detail: AP2 handles the transaction. UCP maintains the cart. Klarna provides the credential. Amazon provides the inventory. These are all protocol-layer components that operate within the app ecosystem. D0 is the discovery layer that feeds intent into that ecosystem before any protocol activates. The OEM-embedded architecture that enables D0 is not competitive with AP2 or UCP — it is upstream of both. A user who sees a lockscreen commerce card and taps will enter a protocol-layer checkout flow. D0 is what made them tap.

ideas.intro:
The Agent Payments Protocol went live May 20, 2026. Google's Universal Commerce Protocol now spans 5,294 stores. Amazon's autonomous Alexa for Shopping executes purchases end-to-end. Stripe's Agentic Commerce Suite gives every AI agent a payment credential layer. The infrastructure of agentic commerce is being assembled in real time, piece by piece, protocol by protocol.

Every piece has the same dependency: user consent at the app layer.

Amazon requires you to authorize Alexa to purchase on your behalf. Klarna in ChatGPT requires you to connect your account. Google AP2 requires you to establish payment credentials within the Google ecosystem. The consent step is correct from a privacy standpoint. It is also the friction point that every agentic commerce system is racing to minimize — and none have eliminated.

Glance eliminated it at the OEM layer. Pre-installed on 175M+ Samsung and Motorola devices at device manufacture, with consent established during device setup rather than app install, Glance's lockscreen commerce surface is present before any app choice, any agent authorization, or any protocol enrollment occurs. That is not a UX optimization. It is a fundamentally different consent architecture — and it is the infrastructure advantage that no agentic protocol launched in 2026 has replicated.
